title: Canonical pullback is bijective in curve degrees zero and one
statement: Let k contained in K be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], f:C over k a smooth separated connected curve [def-sc-curves], and c a smooth connected proper compactification with finite closed boundary [lem-sc-compactification]. Let n be positive and nonzero in k. Let r in each degree be the canonical cohomology pullback followed by the constant-sheaf comparison [def-sc-field-extension], with coefficients Z/n [def-sc-mu-trivialization]. For every integer q with 0 <= q <= 1, r in degree q is bijective.

source.place: proof, proper and affine cases, degrees 0 and 1

proof.text: Use baseChange_curve to obtain the smooth connected curve over K. Split into proper and affine cases by the proper-or-affine dichotomy. Choose a primitive root in k; its image is primitive in K. The primitive-root trivializations commute with pullback, and transport the canonical map to the roots-of-unity comparison.

In degree zero, sections are the nth roots of unity in the ground field. Every root is a unique power of the chosen primitive root, and extension sends that power to the corresponding power. Consequently the pullback in these coordinates is the identity.

For proper C, the units are the ground-field units and are n-divisible; the Kummer sequence identifies H1(mu_n) with Pic(C)[n]. Since integer degree is torsion-free this torsion lies in Picard degree zero. The Jacobian representing isomorphism identifies it with the Jacobian n-torsion points; genus/Jacobian base change and the abelian-variety estimate say their canonical extension map is bijective. Kummer naturality identifies this map with cohomology pullback.

For affine C, affine cohomology gives the short exact degree-one Kummer sequence. Its units-quotient map is bijective by units_quotient_base_change and its Picard-torsion map is bijective by the affine clause of kummer_base_change_compatibility. The short five lemma makes the degree-one map bijective. The degree-zero calculation is already done.

theorem IsConnectedCurve.constant_low_degree_baseChange_bijective
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed K] [Algebra k K]
    {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [Smooth c.g]
    (_hfin : (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ.Finite)
    (_hclosed : ∀ x ∈ (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ, IsClosed ({x} : Set c.Z))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (_hn : (n : k) ≠ 0)
    (r : ∀ q : ℕ, Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod n) q →+
        Sheaf.H ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).constantZMod n) q)
    (hr : (∀ q : ℕ, r q =
        (Sheaf.H.map (((Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))).app
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n)))).hom) q).comp
          (Etale.cohomologyMap
            (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
            (C.constantZMod n) q))) :
    ∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ 1 → Function.Bijective (r q)
